commits.message:
fix(daemon): a launcher pipe event leaves the daemon's facts once no bar can show it (#934)

* fix(daemon): a launcher pipe event leaves the daemon's facts once no bar can show it

The launcher reports each pipe event to its observer and keeps none of it.
The daemon holds the latest in a held slot, as it holds a renderer's end and
an act's failure: shown by the one event hold, answered by a confirmed write,
and let go once no bar can show it. A pipe event that recurs while one is
held is counted, and what recurred is held afresh when the slot lets go, so
a flood moves no bar.

The daemon's facts carry the pipe event as its own field, so the private
renderer wire moves to version 15.

* fix(daemon): each pipe event is held and counted on its own

A pipe event that recurred while another was held used to be folded into
the held one, so a different event was misnamed or never reached a bar.
Pipe events and task throws are now one family of recurring events, held
per subject: an occurrence while its subject is held is counted, and the
latest is held afresh with its count when the slot lets go.

The daemon's facts carry its held events as one list the renderer judges
by the one hold, the launcher's lifeline warning is a single value, the
launcher's unused instant is gone, and both kinds say how often they
recurred in the same words.

* fix(daemon): recurring events close with their owner and stamp one way

A closed family of recurring events takes no occurrence, so a pipe event
that lands after close arms no end on a closed daemon. The family stamps
every event it shows at the instant it is shown, a first occurrence and a
recurrence alike, where a task throw used to carry the instant it was
caught. The wording of a recurrence moves to the event hold with the rest of
the events' vocabulary, and the hold-end task is named from the kind.

The draw tells an error from a warning once, and names what a standing
warning is about beside the warning, not by whether it has a subject. The
frame record names each pipe event's hold.

* fix(daemon): a daemon event is always about something

Every event of the daemon's own carries what it is about, a kind that holds
one event at a time being about itself, so the feed's cover of an answer and
the owner's acknowledgement of it ask one question of an event's identity.
A recurring subject is held only when its slot holds, so a subject whose event
could not be built is shown by its next occurrence. What a diagnostic is
about is built in one place, the repository question included.

fix(config): one key classifier, one write router, and Back steps that end with their edit

What a session key is (edit mode's own, a setting, a confirm, the
viewer, a menu, an author's) is decided by one function, and every
reader and writer switches on it. Every session write passes one
router: an open edit holds it, and with none open edit mode's keys are
set aside for the edit a click opens, or dropped and logged. An edit
holds the Back steps taken in it, and the click that ends it lands its
own step outside, without edit mode's keys. Whether an edit has work is
the files it changed and the drafts a save writes, one count for the
save cell, cancel and the idle close. The duplicate-id hint is fixed
text, the click error reads only records this build writes, and a
session left empty by the load takes no slot.

fix(config): decide edit-or-store once per click and check authored keys wherever they load

A click outside an edit holds edit mode's keys aside: they open the edit
it starts, or are dropped and logged at warn. Every reader takes the
edit's view, the main undo never records an edit key, and drafts are
neither main-undo nor navigation state. A closed edit's steps are never
Back destinations because its state never reaches the store.

The authored-key check runs for plugins too, refuses raw keys by
namespace and accordion keys only where they meet the bar's own. The
click error lives under the settings namespace. Hover text decodes menu
keys. Minted placement ids retry a bounded number of times and throw.
fix(config): give re-added placements a fresh id and keep edit-mode state in the edit

fix(settings): fold every pick through one setting table and warn on stale picks

A session pick its setting can no longer hold (an uninstalled or retired theme, an undeclared style or preset, a dropped effect, an out-of-range value, a placement value outside its declaration) now reads through its setting's one parse as stale. The fold draws what lies beneath it and reports which rung decided, and the frame shows one stale warning per stale pick that decided, naming the setting, the spelling held, what the bar wears and what the setting can hold. Every save releases every pick that is not a draft against the config it wrote, and a state variable may no longer read a setting's session key.
